findings.title: Incorrect permission check: AND instead of OR for team admin/owner
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, requiring the user to be BOTH admin and owner simultaneously. This is logically wrong — a team admin who is not the owner (or vice versa) will be denied, defeating the purpose of the variable name. This likely blocks legitimate team admins from adding guests unless they also happen to be the owner.

findings.title: Blacklist filtering is case-sensitive mismatch
findings.body: Blacklisted emails are lowercased (`blacklistedGuestEmails`), but `guests` input emails are compared as-is without lowercasing (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). If a user submits an email in a different case than the blacklist entry, the blacklist check silently fails to filter it out.

findings.title: EventManager built with wrong user credentials
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches credentials for the requesting user, but the booking's calendar should be updated using the organizer's (booking owner's) credentials, not necessarily the current ctx user (who could be an attendee or team admin per the earlier permission check). This can cause calendar updates to fail silently or use wrong calendar accounts when the acting user differs from the booking owner.

findings.title: New guest attendees created with empty name
findings.body: Guests added via this flow get `name: ""` persisted to the attendees table, unlike organically-booked attendees which typically have proper names. This could break UI elements and emails that rely on attendee.name (e.g., `FirstAttendee`/`Attendee` components fall back to email when name is falsy, but other consumers of attendee data may not handle empty string gracefully).

findings.title: Email send failures silently swallowed without proper logging
findings.body: The catch block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging the actual error (`err`) or using the structured logger used elsewhere in the codebase (`@calcom/lib/logger`). This makes debugging failed guest-notification emails difficult in production.

findings.title: Zod schema recreated on every render
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is created inside the component body on every render instead of being hoisted to module scope. This is a minor but unnecessary recomputation on every re-render of the dialog.

findings.title: Empty string guest input passes validation incorrectly
findings.body: `multiEmailValue` is initialized as `[""]` and the dialog allows submitting with default state. `z.array(z.string().email())` will reject an empty string, so this particular case would fail, but if a user removes rows down to zero entries the `handleAdd` early-returns only on `length === 0`; however there's no guard preventing submission with duplicate/trimmed whitespace-only entries which may pass or fail inconsistently with server-side validation (`z.string().email()` in addGuests.schema.ts), causing inconsistent UX between client validation message and server error.
